This is Traceback, an incident investigator whose answers you can check, not just trust. It uses Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory.
A simulated outage in a small backend. Sixty-four of twenty-three hundred checkout requests are failing, and the loudest dashboard points at payments. Where would you look?

The obvious tool is to paste the raw logs into the same model. It answers payments, with high confidence and a tidy explanation. The simulator knows the truth: orders, a retry storm. The confident answer is wrong.

Traceback measures first. It aligns clocks, correlates spans into traces, and ranks candidate causes, each tied to evidence. The model only explains those candidates. Every citation is checked, and the incident is replayed with the suspected cause switched off. Five of six stages use no model.
Here is the same outage. Orders, retry amplification, is the top candidate, and every claim in the chain cites a record that exists. You can open each one and read it.

Then the replay. With the cause on, eleven percent of requests fail. Switch the retry storm off, and it drops to one percent. The other candidates stay inconclusive. Only a cause the replay confirms can be reported with high confidence.

It is not always right. In this incident, the analyzer had the correct answer, payments, but the model overruled it and chose orders. The replay could not confirm that, so the confidence is medium, not high. Being wrong and saying so is the point.

On forty-eight fresh simulated incidents, Traceback finds the cause ninety-six percent of the time, against sixty-nine for raw logs. It is never confidently wrong, where the baseline is, twenty-nine percent of the time, at a tenth of the cost. These are our own simulators, so this shows the method, not production accuracy.

On real R C A Eval data, the picture is more modest. On code faults in unseen systems, the baseline gets fourteen of sixty and our hybrid twenty-two, with confident wrong answers cut from nineteen to one. The larger Ultra model goes from nineteen to thirty-eight. The hand-written analyzer does not generalize, and every wrong answer is listed in the repository.
An answer you can check beats one you have to trust. Everything reproduces offline, with no A P I key. The code is at github dot com slash Actually Anson slash Traceback.
